record.reason: The inspection of surface defects in leather manufacture has attracted considerable attention due to the significant impact of appearance on leather pricing. In order to address the challenges associated with leather defect inspection, this study presents a comprehensive deep learning framework for classifying surface defects on leather materials. The proposed framework integrates a convolutional neural network for binary descriptor extraction with a dual channel transformer for classification. The binary descriptor reduces computational complexity while preserving discriminative feature representations. The computational benefit of the binary representation can be quantified as follows. With the binary descriptor, each element is either 0 or 1, so multiplications are replaced by simple bitwise AND operations, and additions are replaced by bitwise population count (POPCNT) instructions. In practice, considering memory access patterns and the overhead of binarization, the measured speedup in the attention mechanism is approximately 8x to 12x compared with floating point features of the same dimensionality., and the dual channel transformer captures both spatial and temporal information from the extracted features. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves competitive performance with mean accuracy of 94.87 percent, mean sensitivity of 95.43 percent, and mean specificity of 94.60 percent on the manually collected dataset, together with mean accuracy of 94.14 percent on the publicly available dataset.
